chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is entrusted with judging, let him be equitable between them in his gestures, his gaze, and his seating.'

key_terms.النَّظَر: gaze/looking — the direction and manner of a judge's eye contact with litigants
key_terms.الْإِشَارَة: gesture/indication — the way a judge uses hand or body signals during proceedings
key_terms.الْقَضَاء: judicial office/judging — the formal role of a qadi (judge) in Islamic law
key_terms.الْمَجْلِس: sitting/session — the arrangement of seats in the court; treating parties unequally in seating is itself a form of bias

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about how a judge should treat litigants equally in court?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) lays down a foundational principle for judicial conduct: a judge must maintain complete equality between litigants in every non-verbal dimension — gestures, eye contact, and seating arrangement. This teaching reflects the Islamic legal tradition that justice is not merely a matter of the verdict, but of the entire judicial demeanor; partiality shown through body language or preferential seating was recognized as a form of injustice that could intimidate or demean one party. The original audience of jurists and Muslim rulers would have understood this as a comprehensive ethical code, going beyond verbal impartiality to guard against subtle biases.
